name: Gaztelumendi breach – Larrabetzu Iron Belt bunker
story: The Iron Belt was built from late 1936 as a ring of trenches, bunkers and gun positions around Bilbao. It was planned for about 70,000 defenders but held by roughly 30,000, and the engineer Alejandro Goicoechea defected to the Nationalists with its plans, revealing its weak points. On 12 June 1937 the Nationalists concentrated heavy artillery and more than a hundred aircraft on the weak Gaztelumendi sector at Larrabetzu and broke through. A last Basque counter-attack at Mantuliz (Derio) failed, and Bilbao fell a week later. Near Sarrikola a concrete bunker was built into a farmhouse; ongoing excavations here have uncovered more remains of the line.
see: A Civil War bunker built inside a building in the Sarrikola area, near the Gaztelumendi breach sector.
plan: In the rural Sarrikola neighbourhood of Larrabetzu. Treat it as private property and look from the lane; combine it with the Zamudio Iron Belt trail on the same ridge.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
